bearings.paper_claim: SMOreg on standardized LIWC and MRCPD features per member-year; scores relative to the Congressional Record (fn 10); 100 sentence-level bootstraps per member-year; CI width about 0.3 or less above about 5,000 words a year (median member about 11,000 words); optional jackknife over other years.
bearings.system_side: big5_traits.py follows the steps: corpus-standardized features and z-scores relative to this corpus (about lines 236-251); default speech sources CREC and INTERVIEW (lines 36-40); lowconf below LOWCONF_TOKENS=1500 (lines 28, 251); N = -ES (line 22). The docstring (lines 13-16) also says the license-bound SMOreg file is replaced by published-correlate linear weights, a fourth deviation the analyst omitted. The RKH refit exists in fit_smoreg_rkh.py (5-fold held-out r), but no stored output with the .350 figure was found.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Transfers as a procedure only. The paper's precision band assumes about 11,000 words per member-year; the 1,500-token floor is far below the paper's 5,000-word band, so the precision claim does not transfer. Refitting to RKH makes RKH convergence a fit statistic, not validation.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers and page locations hold. Code steps verified in big5_traits.py. The .350 held-out r is unverified in stored output. The omitted linear-weights substitution is added to system_side.

bearings.paper_claim: Conscientiousness lowers the ceremonial share of sponsored bills: -0.52 (M1), -0.39 (M3), -0.53 (M4), -0.58 (M5, Congress FE), all p<0.01. Majority x C is +0.27 (M4) and +0.29 (M5), so the C effect is smallest in the majority. N = 3,648 member-Congresses in M3 to M5, 104th to 112th Congresses; binomial regression with implicit weighting by bills proposed (fn 37).
bearings.system_side: lep_criterion.py computes Spearman rho between pooled ceremonial share (115th to 118th Congresses, at least 8 bills) and diligence_z, lexical C v1 and behaviour-calibrated C v2. Stored data/members/lep_criterion.json: rho 0.0026, 0.0176 and 0.0003, n = 440, all null. There is no majority split. The script's own comment (lines 127-128) says the test is attenuated.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's effect is minority-concentrated, so a pooled rank correlation is an UNSTRATIFIED test of a conditional claim. Modern Congresses carry few ceremonial bills, which attenuates the test. A stratified, bill-weighted re-run is new analysis and stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it.
bearings.verifier_note: Table 3 coefficients verified. N = 3,648 applies to M3 to M5 only (M1 is 3,736), and the weighting is implicit trial weighting, not a bill-weighted regression. System side verified against the stored JSON.

bearings.paper_claim: The 2016 paper's only Conscientiousness outcome is the ceremonial-bill share (Table 3). It has no roll-call participation analysis; roll calls appear only in passing as a source of ideal points (p.5).
bearings.paper_location: pp.5, 15-18, Table 3; full-text search found no participation outcome
bearings.system_side: behavioral_dispositions.py docstring (lines 13-14) calls diligence_z, which is roll-call participation, RKH's strongest C criterion. diligence_z is now the mean of participation and LEP follow-through (lines 49-71).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The 2016 text does not support the attribution. Whether another RKH work (the 2015 manuscripts cited at pp.15 and 19) uses participation cannot be checked from this text. Treat as a citation fix, not a modelling finding.
bearings.verifier_note: Verified that the 2016 paper has no participation analysis, so the citation as written is unsupported by this source. The contradicts relation holds only at citation level.

bearings.paper_claim: The paper has no direct validation against ground-truth personality measures for legislators. Its validity rests on ideology correlations (Table 1 Model 1, R2 0.10, N 844), LIWC face validity, NPAT response and bill shares. For NPAT, Emotional Stability moves predicted response from about 30 to about 53 percent between -2 and +2 SD (Table 2 Model 4, N 598). The paper says this suggests selection bias; it does not show it.
bearings.system_side: The analyst's description of Senate expert and insider panels, pre-registered single looks and the E/A/O/N/C pattern could not be verified. Brain topic lines 25-32 cite RKH results, not panels. The cited code path is wrong; the file is at fec/members/big5_improvements_eval.py and contains no panel code found by grep.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Senate panels against a House paper is a cross-chamber assumption. The paper's NPAT argument concerns self-report surveys, not expert ratings, so it does not directly apply to the panels.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claim verified except that the paper says suggests, not shows. System-side panel results are unverified and the code path needs correcting.

bearings.paper_claim: Emotional Stability's link to anxiety words is somewhat weaker than those for Openness, Conscientiousness and Extraversion (p.11). Agreeableness is also described as weaker (p.11). ES predicts survey response (Table 2) and loads 0.20 (p<0.01) on Common Space in Table 1 Model 1.
bearings.system_side: N = -ES is carried over (big5_traits.py:22). Affective N is E-residualized and party-controlled (emit_affective_n.py:39-59). Brain topic record 6 reports raw r -0.11 (E-cleaned -0.04, not significant) against RKH-ES at n 147, and broad text-N -0.22. The interview-to-floor rho values (.050, .161) were not checked.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's weak ES-anxiety link is a face-validity remark, not a ranking of ES as weakest. Party-residualizing may remove ES signal that the paper's ideology check carries.
bearings.verifier_note: 'Weakest' is not the paper's word: it names O, C and E as stronger, and A as also weaker. The system-side correlations match the brain record.

bearings.paper_claim: Conscientiousness acts like a discount factor (fn 35), but fn 35 attributes that model to a separate Ramey, Klingler and Hollibaugh 2015 manuscript. Within this paper, more Conscientious minority members are less deterred by partisan obstacles because they weight future payoffs (pp.15-16); the C effect is smallest for the majority (p.18).
bearings.system_side: receptivity_layer.py: behavioural basis SUSC_z = .40 coop + .30 N - .20 diligence - .10 dominance (line 173); lexical basis .40 A + .30 N - .20 C - .10 E (line 186). Neither branch has a majority-status term. The code comment calls the weights local calibration, not a design prior.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper concerns bill-type choice, not response to lobbying pressure, so transfer is analogical. Conditioning C on majority status would be a new proposal with no validation behind it.
bearings.verifier_note: Code formulas verified. The discount-factor source is a companion manuscript, not this text. The design prior wording is the analyst's; the code says local calibration.

summary_issues: Year: the item and summary say 2016 (DOI 10.1017/psrm.2016.12; text header 2016). Birkenmaier cites the same article as PSRM 7(1) 2019 pp.163-184 (print). Keep 2016 as online date and confirm citation metadata before filing.

summary_md says the paper gives no grounds for treating the published RKH scores as ground truth. The paper never discusses RKH scores; it only promises to release its own scores on publication (fn 16). The sentence should say the paper has no ground-truth validation of its scores.

summary_md says the speechwriter defence covers floor speech only and not tweets or interviews. That exclusion is the analyst's inference; the paper's defence is generic to speeches and does not address other genres.
summary_md gives Table 3 N = 3,648 for the whole table. It applies to Models 3 to 5; Model 1 has 3,736 and Model 2 has 3,732.
